purpose: Bind the Core5 setting-board briefs to already researched historical/current/trajectory evidence while separating research fact, fiction translation, future trajectory and OPEN details.

researchEvidence: Postwar rationing of food and daily necessities continued while delays and missed distribution occurred.
Urban households could rely on shopping trips and black markets in addition to formal distribution.
Clothing and ordinary goods were repaired and kept in use rather than assuming easy replacement.
Paper coupons, ledgers and incomplete records are appropriate system evidence for the era band.
Housing shortage, temporary/incomplete housing and public-health friction can appear as background conditions without making every scene misery.
Postwar school-lunch recovery and changing food access are real research context, but do not define Tomori's literal school history.

researchEvidence: Rapid heavy-industry growth and urbanization in the 1960s produced serious industrial-pollution and health problems, followed by stronger countermeasures in the 1970s.
The 1973 oil shock exposed Japan's high oil dependence and produced supply anxiety, inflation and buying panic.
Road, rail, new-town and older-neighborhood systems could coexist during development rather than one cleanly replacing another.
Household prosperity and energy/price pressure can coexist; the era is not visually equivalent to universal poverty.
Diet diversified with greater meat, dairy, oil, instant and processed-food presence alongside continued rice-centered meals.

researchEvidence: The employment-ice-age context spans roughly the 1993–2004 job-search cohort and left long-running unstable-employment/social-participation effects.
In 2002, household access to Internet-capable devices was expanding but not universal; PC and mobile/PHS access coexisted.
By 2005 Internet-capable household-device ownership had increased further, showing a fast transition rather than an always-online settled norm.
Feature phones, PHS, mobile mail, PC mail, BBS/personal sites, handles, printouts and FAX are appropriate early-network evidence.
Printed maps and online information can coexist; reply delay and disconnected time remain ordinary.
Convenience-store/prepared food and abundance are ordinary context; shortage is not the era's default food story.

researchEvidence: Government guidance in 2026 treats online false/misleading information, AI-generated fake images and deepfakes as practical verification problems.
A 2025 national loneliness/isolation survey reported that roughly four in ten respondents experienced some loneliness, so constant connectivity may coexist with isolation.
The 2025 aging-society white paper reports an aging rate of 29.3% and continued growth of older people living alone.
Prepared/ready-made meals support busy daily life while food access can still be difficult because of aging, retail decline, low income and other constraints, including in urban contexts.
Smartphones, group chat, cloud photo, cashless/QR-like payment, delivery/takeout and recommendation systems are ordinary present-day infrastructure but do not define every person's access equally.

researchEvidence: Japan's Moonshot Goal 1 researches a 2050 direction involving robotic/avatar embodiment, expanded ability/perception and reduced body/space/time constraints.
Current Digital Agency trust work treats digital identity and authenticity/non-tampering of data as real infrastructure questions.
Current AI-governance work emphasizes human-centered governance, safety and transparency.
These present-day trajectories are research anchors only; they do not prove the exact Far Future society in Yoru-no-Shirube.
